clue.text: Reading giving a lot of pleasure when reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed here means looked over afresh, so the letters are recast in a new order
a lot of, not all, means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A book that brings great enjoyment each time someone goes back over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last E of PLEASURE to leave PLEASUR; 'when reviewed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful read through a text, so the noun stands for reading.

clue.text: A marker kept by river in a wild and remote region

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the next word

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a tag is a label marking something

indicators.note: wild means the letters of in a run riot

explanation.surface: A label held by a river somewhere untamed and far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like part of the definition but turns IN A into NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the sparsely populated southern tip of South America.

clue.text: Actor scanned in audience old director

indicators.note: an audience hears things, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: to scan a text is to read it
John Ford was a classic Hollywood director

explanation.surface: A performer read over by a veteran filmmaker in front of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: READ in the past tense is said like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Redford is an American film star.

clue.text: Novel about royal wife, mean-spirited woman

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the next piece

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A book about a king's spouse, a spiteful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal but names the book She.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging woman.

clue.text: Educational body felt to be corrupt in paper

parts.note: LEA is a British Local Education Authority

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A school authority believed to be crooked in a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out to inform people.

clue.text: Mention of island tree

indicators.note: a mention is something spoken, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: Talk of an island famous for one particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypress is a tall evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Venue for operating PCs?

parts.note: PCs here are police constables, not personal computers, and the venue is their base of operations

explanation.surface: A place where personal computers are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop shop is slang for a police station.

clue.text: Devious note in part worried influential fellow

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
devious means twisting, so the letters of note are rearranged

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A scheming memo in which a powerful man was partly troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' gives the anagram ONET; 'worried' is the slangy sense of 'eaten', as in what's eating you.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a ruler or powerful person.

clue.text: Hotel might offer this version of iTunes with an echo

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Echo is the radio code word for E

explanation.surface: A hotel might provide a remixed music app with reverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with its own attached bathroom is described as en suite.

clue.text: Quiet bar lacking note? It betrays indifference

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing

parts.note: a rung is a bar of a ladder

explanation.surface: A silent pub without music shows someone doesn't care.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug of the shoulders signals that someone doesn't care.

clue.text: Detour arranged to avoid front of exposed house

indicators.note: arranged means the remaining letters are put in a new order
to avoid says a letter is kept out of the word detour
front of picks the first letter of the word exposed

explanation.surface: A diversion planned so as not to pass an unprotected house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' takes E (the 'front of exposed') out of DETOUR, leaving DTOUR; 'arranged' reorders it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Preliminary dish, favourite amid praise for cooking

indicators.note: amid says one piece sits in the middle of the other
cooking means the letters of praise are worked into a new mix

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A starter in which a favourite ingredient is surrounded by compliments to the chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' gives the anagram APISER, and 'amid' splits it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser is a small starter served before the main course.

clue.text: Film appealing to Shakespearean sleuths?

parts.note: detectives on the trail of the Bard would be searching for a kindly Shakespeare: the title of a 1997 film read literally

explanation.surface: A movie that detectives with a taste for Shakespeare would enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's first name is Will, so a hunt for 'good Will' is what Shakespearean sleuths would be on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1997 film starring Matt Damon about a gifted janitor.

clue.text: Certainly a misrepresentation of Thomas's position?

explanation.surface: An assured remark that gets a doubting apostle's stance badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection unseen, held the opposite view.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainly means without question; the opposite of doubt would misstate the sceptical apostle Thomas.

clue.text: Inferior foreign articles left in Bag End

parts.note: un is a French article and der a German one
der is German for the

indicators.note: End picks the last letter of Bag

explanation.surface: A lowly hobbit's foreign goods abandoned at Bilbo's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Bag End is the hobbit home in Tolkien, but here only its final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a subordinate, someone of lower rank.

clue.text: Doctor in lead beginning to order substance in trial?

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to doctor a drink is to lace it

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word order

explanation.surface: A medic in charge starting to prescribe something in a clinical test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb, to adulterate.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert dose given to a control group in a drug trial.

clue.text: Science in which pupils might be assessed?

definitions.text: Science in which pupils might be assessed?

parts.words: Science in which pupils might be assessed?
parts.note: the pupils are parts of the eye, not schoolchildren, and the testing is of eyesight

explanation.surface: A school subject in which students get tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Optometry is the profession of examining eyes and prescribing lenses.

clue.text: Operatic heroine in part of opera before turn in finale

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: an aria is a solo song within an opera

indicators.note: turn in says the word for finale is read backwards

parts.note: a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A soprano role featured in a section of an opera ahead of a twist at the close.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne is the title character of Strauss's opera Ariadne auf Naxos.

clue.text: A couple of married soldiers are staying in the Italian base

indicators.note: staying in means housed inside the next word

parts.note: il is Italian for the
M for married twice
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
an are is a metric unit of area, A

explanation.surface: Two wedded troops are lodged in an Italian military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but is the adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as an adjective means morally low, wicked.

clue.text: Plaintive writer on island in film

indicators.note: in says these go inside the next word

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film
on and leg are both the same side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A mournful author appearing on an island in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful poems.

clue.text: One waiting with little time for Dutch expert on circuits?

indicators.note: for means one letter replaces another

parts.note: a steward waits on passengers or diners
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A waiter who takes a short break in place of a Dutch colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with little time for Dutch' swaps D in STEWARD for T. Jackie Stewart was a three-time Formula One world champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing driver is an expert on motor-racing circuits, as the Scottish champion was.

clue.text: Dog someday straying

indicators.note: straying means wandering off, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: A hound that will wander off one of these days.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samoyed is a white Siberian sled dog breed.

clue.text: Gain a hundred with place buzzing around end of game

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the next piece

parts.note: a hive is a place buzzing with bees

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of game

explanation.surface: Score a century with the ground buzzing at the close of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to attain or win something through effort.

clue.text: Writer recreating rummest home saga

indicators.note: recreating means making anew, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: An author reworking a very odd family chronicle.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Somerset Maugham was an English novelist and playwright.

clue.text: School diet after reform put in place

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
reform means reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school's menu, once overhauled, gets established.
explanation.definitionFit: Sited means located or positioned somewhere.

clue.text: Extremist taking part in awful traditions

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A radical joining in with dreadful customs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views.

clue.text: Sluggish quality I had detected in depressed place defended by Conservative

indicators.note: defended by means surrounded by the political word that follows

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: detected in says the contraction is found inside the next word

parts.note: a pit is a hollow in the ground
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A lethargic manner the speaker spotted in a gloomy area guarded by a right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'detected in' builds PIDIT first, and 'defended by' then wraps the party word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpidity is the state of being torpid, that is sluggishness or inactivity.

clue.text: River and fast stream churning out gold

indicators.note: out says these letters are removed

parts.note: a torrent is a fast, churning stream
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A river with a rushing current that has lost its gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.

clue.text: Transport to leave in the dark?

explanation.surface: Taking someone away so as to strand them without a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DE- (removing) plus LIGHT, it means to plunge into darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport is to enrapture, a meaning shared with delight; the second sense is a joke on removing illumination.

clue.text: Commercial figure engaged in measure to back fabrics

indicators.note: to back means the whole combination is turned round
engaged in means held inside the next word

parts.note: a yard is a unit of length
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman involved in a scheme to support textile makers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns round the whole of YREPARD, the container built by 'engaged in', not just the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapery is cloth or textiles, especially those hung in folds.
